template:
Fresh blind reader {ROLE}. Read ONLY your assigned frozen summary-snapshot.md and questions.json, and read/write your own reader-{role}-draft.json, reader-{role}-self-check.json and reader-{role}.json. No source rules, keys/scopes, earlier outputs/grades/history, web, outside game knowledge, session logs, collaboration/status tools, scratch files or other inputs.

INITIAL DELIVERY: Use the supplied absolute input paths directly, with python3 where needed. Do not list directories, discover files or inspect other metadata. Before ANY output write, visibly receive EVERY summary line in chunks <=45 lines and EVERY complete question object in chunks <=6. Each chunk must have its OWN functions.exec response; print plain tool output and JSON ensure_ascii=False. Read the actual question count and final ID. Recover any truncation before drafting.

VERSIONED HIERARCHICAL SOURCE UNITS: Derive units ONLY from the frozen summary. Recognize column-zero headings with one through six '#' characters, one space, and a nonempty title. Level-one headings close lower-level units but are not selectable. This lexer explicitly does not support fenced code; if present report the technical issue rather than silently interpreting it. Never reuse an old H-number for a larger range.

For each selectable heading (levels2–6), provide two DISTINCT units:
- T plus its zero-padded physical start line: the COMPLETE SUBTREE, from the heading through all deeper descendant headings/procedures, ending immediately before the next recognized heading of equal or higher level, or EOF.
- I plus its start line: the COMPLETE INTRODUCTION, ending immediately before the next recognized heading of ANY level, or EOF. An introduction is not a complete parent subtree.

Generic Python index algorithm (no question routing):
    heads = list(re.finditer(r'(?m)^(#{1,6}) (.+)$', summary_text))
    for index, match in enumerate(heads):
        level = len(match.group(1))
        if level == 1: continue
        start = match.start()
        line = summary_text[:start].count('\n') + 1
        intro_end = heads[index+1].start() if index+1 < len(heads) else len(summary_text)
        subtree_end = next((h.start() for h in heads[index+1:] if len(h.group(1)) <= level), len(summary_text))
        for prefix, kind, end in [('I','introduction',intro_end),('T','subtree',subtree_end)]:
            section_id = prefix + str(line).zfill(3)
            section_text = summary_text[start:end]
            heading = match.group()
            start_offset, end_offset = start, end  # Unicode character offsets, end exclusive
            start_line = line
            end_line = line + section_text.count('\n') - (1 if section_text.endswith('\n') else 0)
            sha256 = hashlib.sha256(section_text.encode()).hexdigest()

Choose the smallest appropriate NONOVERLAPPING units that supply all asked facts and qualifiers. A broad procedure can require its parent subtree. A narrow request can use complete introductions plus relevant child subtrees; include necessary ancestor/shared conditions, external definitions and exceptions. An explicit union that omits siblings must not be labeled a complete parent. Do not select a parent subtree together with an overlapping child, or duplicate leaf introduction/subtree aliases. Adjacent intervals are allowed. Selected source slices must be copied in source order. Unit IDs and heading/ancestor metadata are source locations, not answers or per-question recommendations.

IDENTIFIED ATTACHMENTS: Put each selected unit into answer exactly once using these exact delimiters:
    begin = '<!-- qa-unit:' + section_id + ':begin -->\n'
    end = '<!-- qa-unit:' + section_id + ':end -->'
    identified_block = begin + section_text + end
Preserve the FULL EXACT source slice including heading, all descendants for a subtree, all tables/lists, final conditions/outcomes and trailing whitespace. Do not crop or trim it. Source must not contain the reserved '<!-- qa-unit:' marker; if it does, report the technical issue. Metadata records the source slice's untrimmed hash. Unit-ID-aware attachment checks remain structural, separate from factual grading.

MODEL CHOICE, TOOL COPYING ONLY: You must choose each question's governing procedure, relevant sections and supporting facts by reading and understanding its wording and the source. Do not create automated question-to-section matching, sentence ranking, keyword/phrase routing or a code-generated unsupported fallback. Code may index the generic source headings, copy the exact sections/spans YOU selected, serialize JSON and check literal matches. A failed string lookup or empty search hit is a locator error, not proof the rule is absent. Reread and correct the locator; never turn a lookup failure into an unsupported answer. Complete each question semantically before writing its source-selection data.

Work on EXACTLY ONE QUESTION AT A TIME after the complete initial read. Visibly reread that question and every chosen complete unit in bounded <=45-line chunks before composing its entry. Finish its individual semantic requests and written source choices before proceeding to the next question. Code may append/serialize that one completed entry to your own partial draft; never fill missing choices with a default first/overview/reference section or a template. A missing manual choice is unfinished work, not a completed answer. Before selecting sections, split each question into its individual actual requests. A compound question must not become one unsplit ledger item with a whole section substituted as its fact. Build an ordered clause_ledger. Each requested_clause is an exact phrase from the question. For each actor, condition, exception, cost, quantity, destination, timing, sequence or outcome, identify the actual source fact that answers THAT request.

For ordinary rule facts, supply a SHORT FAITHFUL fact in your own words or copy a SHORT EXACT supporting sentence/table row. Each ledger item has {requested_clause,section_ids,fact_kind:'quote'|'paraphrase'|'unsupported',fact_source_section,supported_fact_or_case_result}. Use fact_kind=quote only for a literal contiguous span inside the declared selected source unit. Use fact_kind=paraphrase for an accurate restatement: its wording need not be literal, but its actor, condition, cost, quantity, destination, timing and outcome must agree with the full source unit. Both kinds must reference the actual selected source supplying that fact. fact_source_section is the bare T/I ID, NEVER full text, a heading title or path. Use additional ledger items when noncontiguous passages or multiple individual requests require them. Do not substitute a whole section or a repeated general paragraph for each individual fact. If the summary genuinely lacks a requested fact, use fact_kind=unsupported and explicitly abstain; never invent, force a guess or substitute a merely related rule. A failed literal locator does not establish absence and does not invalidate a faithful paraphrase.

Read the complete appropriate sections for EACH request visibly in bounded chunks. Select the smallest set that actually supplies ALL requested facts. Follow procedural references, definitions, phase transitions and exceptions into their other source sections when needed; a bare reference does not itself state the referenced operative restrictions. Do not select by keyword frequency or a fixed number of hits. Check the source quote actually answers its own request. Avoid unrelated sections or whole-summary dumps.

ANSWER: Ordinary rule requests are answered by the faithful facts in the ledger and the complete selected source sections. Avoid an additional repeated paraphrase outside the ledger that could change an actor, condition, number or destination. For an explicitly requested concrete legal/yes-no or numerical scenario, put a minimal resolved conclusion and actual calculation in case_conclusions and at the start of answer. case_conclusions is an array of plain strings, with no nested confidence/location metadata. For a general request to list/explain rules, case_conclusions is empty; faithful ledger facts (quote or paraphrase) supply the rules. Every added conclusion must agree with all controlling qualifiers.

Then put 'Applicable summary text' INSIDE answer and attach each selected COMPLETE source unit ONCE using the identified blocks specified above, in source order. Copy the exact slice programmatically after selecting it through the clause ledger. Do not duplicate the long section under both a Direct Answer heading and Applicable Text for volume. Complete all fields faithfully: substantive same-entry facts in ledger, conclusions, answer and operative evidence can count in later content grading; field names/format/support labels alone do not establish correctness. Another question's or reader's facts never supply this entry's omissions. The required complete source attachments and exact quote format are separately checked, not a substitute for substantive requested-fact coverage.

Each entry: {id,clause_ledger:[{requested_clause,section_ids:[...],fact_kind,fact_source_section,supported_fact_or_case_result}],case_conclusions:[...],operative_sections:[{section_id,kind,heading,level,start_offset,end_offset,start_line,end_line,sha256}],answer,support:'supported'|'partial'|'unsupported',evidence:[{summary_location,quote}]}. operative_sections contains metadata only; complete text is in answer. evidence may quote each selected heading, since the full operative section already appears in answer. Top-level {inputs_read:[two absolute paths],answers:[...]}. Preserve the FIRST COMPLETE N-answer draft unchanged as reader-{role}-draft.json; incremental work is allowed only after full initial delivery. Do not retype unchanged sections for final output: load the draft and apply repairs.

UNSUPPORTED-CLAUSE REVIEW: Before preserving an unsupported clause, reread every complete section already attached to that same entry, then the governing definitions, conditions and referenced procedures elsewhere in the frozen summary. Look for the requested meaning, not the question's exact wording. If an operative rule supplies the fact, replace the unsupported statement with the correct faithful ledger fact (quote or paraphrase). Do not retain an abstention beside text that already unambiguously answers it. If the fact is genuinely absent, keep an honest unsupported statement describing the precise remaining unknown and the source contexts checked; do not guess or claim that all answers must be supported.

SELF-CHECK: Write reader-{role}-self-check.json with EVERY ID. Compare its exact question to its own asked-clause ledger. Record each requested clause, actual supplied fact/result, supporting section IDs, and any missing clause, irrelevant section, contradiction or repair. Check all named conditions, actors, destinations and quantities. For EACH individual request, record the question's governing procedure/condition, the selected quote's governing procedure/condition, the actor and the requested outcome or destination. Confirm they match before accepting a quote; a correct rule from a neighboring or differently conditioned procedure is not an answer to this request. A reference to another section requires checking that section's actual restrictions/destinations. Review every abstention explicitly under the unsupported-clause review above, and repair genuine contradictions or omissions; confidence/format labels are not the check. For EVERY quote-kind ledger fact, mechanically verify the exact span in its declared selected source and verify its meaning answers that individual request. For EVERY paraphrase-kind ledger fact, compare its meaning to the COMPLETE declared selected source, including all governing qualifiers; literal wording is not required. Record quote/paraphrase checks separately. Never turn a correct paraphrase into an unsupported claim solely because its wording differs. Do not relabel an inaccurate fact to avoid checking its meaning. Use exact source heading lines in metadata, including Markdown markers. Do not use a whole compound question as a replacement for its individual requests. Ensure case conclusions and calculations agree with operative text and include the controlling exception. Mechanically recompute each selected unit's introduction/subtree boundaries, untrimmed hash and exact identified attachment. Check selected half-open source intervals do not overlap. No partial union may be represented as a whole subtree. A global 'all checked' assertion is insufficient. Repair actual problems in final reader-{role}.json while preserving first complete draft and written check. Final self_review lists all checked IDs, changed IDs/reasons, boundary-check results and self-check filename. Validate all N ordered unique FINAL IDs, actual question-clause phrases, selected source references, quote spans for quote-kind facts, complete copied source text and JSON. Preserve the first complete draft unchanged even if later final ordering or fact revisions are needed. Complete the per-ID self-check and final file for ALL N questions; an honest substantive unknown may remain explicitly recorded, never guessed. Record technical deviations separately; do not stop after a partial batch or return only an input-read/status message. Do not grade against unavailable keys. Final notify only your three paths when all required files cover every ID. Both readers receive this identical generic protocol except role/path; no failed IDs, answer facts, keys or earlier answers.
